title: كيف يتشكّل قوس قزح؟
description: لماذا نرى قوس قزح دائمًا في الجهة المقابلة للشمس، ولماذا يكون على شكل قوس؟ شرح مبسّط للانكسار والتشتّت والانعكاس داخل قطرات المطر.

title: But What Is a Neural Network?
description: 3Blue1Brown's visual introduction to how a neural network recognises handwritten digits, built up from neurons, layers, weights and biases.

title: Fermi Problems
description: Estimating seemingly impossible quantities, like the number of piano tuners in Chicago, with nothing but reasonable assumptions and orders of magnitude.

title: Precision and Recall Without the Confusion
description: Why accuracy misleads on imbalanced data, how precision, recall and F1 differ, and a worked spam-filter example.

title: ما علّمتني إياه حراسة المرمى
description: في كرة القدم لا يتذكّر أحدٌ الحارس إلا عندما يخطئ. ملاحظات قصيرة عن الضغط والتركيز والمسؤولية.

title: How Git Stores Your Code
description: Blobs, trees, commits and references: the small data model behind Git, and why it makes history easier to reason about.

title: Steve Jobs' 2005 Stanford Commencement Address
description: Three short stories about connecting the dots, love and loss, and death, from the speech Steve Jobs gave to Stanford graduates in 2005.

title: Gradient Descent: Lecture Notes
description: The update rule, a fully worked one-dimensional example, choosing a learning rate, mini-batches, and momentum.

title: Astronomy Picture of the Day
description: Every day since 1995, NASA has published one image of the universe with a short explanation written by a professional astronomer.

title: Designing Interfaces That Feel Calm
description: Four habits that make software feel calm: showing less at once, making state obvious, preferring stillness, and staying predictable.

title: The Egg: A Short Story
description: Kurzgesagt's animated adaptation of Andy Weir's short story about life, death, and what it might mean to be everyone.

title: Writing Technical Specifications That Get Read
description: A practical structure for design documents: problem, goals and non-goals, design, alternatives, risks, and rollout.

title: Fitts's Law in Everyday Interfaces
description: The seventy-year-old formula from psychology that explains why big, nearby buttons feel effortless, with a quick worked example.
